input.text: A colleague needs access on our Ubuntu workstation. How do I add a new user account and put that username into a group?
input.subject: How do I add a user to a group?

expected.answer: Add the user account and then add that username to the group. The Users and Groups administration window does the same from the desktop; you need the sudo password to make changes there.

input.text: I have forgotten my Ubuntu login password and cannot get root access to the machine. How do I reset it from recovery mode?
input.subject: Forgot my password

expected.answer: Boot into recovery mode to get a full root shell and reset the forgotten password. Be careful: this step gives full root access to your system and you can damage it.

input.text: What do the read, write and execute permissions actually mean on a directory?
input.subject: Permissions on a shared directory

expected.answer: On a directory, read restricts or allows viewing the directory contents with the ls command, write restricts or allows creating new files or deleting files in the directory, and execute restricts or allows changing into the directory with the cd command. Directories must have execute permissions set or they will not function as folders.

input.text: Coming from another distribution I expected a root account. Why does Ubuntu use sudo instead of letting me log in as root?
input.subject: Why is there no root password?

expected.answer: In Linux there is a SuperUser named root that can do anything and everything, so doing daily work as the SuperUser is dangerous - you could type a command incorrectly and destroy the system. Ideally you run as a regular user that has only the privileges needed for the task at hand and use sudo when root is necessary.

input.text: What counts as a strong password for the accounts on our Ubuntu machines?
input.subject: Password policy guidance

expected.answer: A strong password is at least fifteen characters in length, does not contain your user name, real name, organization name or birth date, does not contain a complete dictionary word, is significantly different from your previous password, and should contain three of the following character types: lowercase alphabetical, uppercase alphabetical, numerics and special characters.

input.text: My wireless connection drops every few minutes and I have to reconnect by hand. Where do I start troubleshooting?
input.subject: Wifi keeps dropping

expected.answer: Recent versions of Ubuntu support most wireless cards. Start from the Wireless Networking Central pages: check the list of supported wireless cards and adapters, then work through getting started, connections and troubleshooting.

input.text: How do I turn on the firewall on an Ubuntu server that I only reach over ssh?
input.subject: Enable the firewall

expected.answer: Append the ssh rule before you enable the firewall: if you enable the firewall under ssh without the ssh rule you will close the ssh connection. Use the command sudo ufw enable ssh from a terminal on the remote computer.

input.text: Can someone explain in plain terms what DNS does on a home network?
input.subject: What does DNS actually do?

expected.answer: DNS is essentially like an internet phone book. Computers on the internet are identified by IPs, which are a string of numbers, and people do not memorize IPs - we memorize domain names. The perfect example of a domain name is google.com.

input.text: After upgrading the release, where does NetworkManager keep the connection configuration files on disk?
input.subject: Where are my network settings stored?

expected.answer: From Ubuntu 23.10 onwards NetworkManager includes netplan, and all the connection configuration files are stored as yaml files in /etc/netplan. If it is not managing your network connections you can remove the .nmconnection files.

input.text: I want to install Ubuntu on a new laptop. How do I make a bootable USB flash drive?
input.subject: Create a bootable USB

expected.answer: To create a USB installation device you need an 8 GB USB flash drive, or a 4 GB device with some of the methods if the iso file is smaller than 4 GB. Files on this USB device will be erased, so backup the files you want to keep before making the device bootable.

input.text: How do I change the GRUB boot menu options, and what applies the change?
input.subject: Change the boot menu

expected.answer: Configuration changes are normally made to the /etc/default/grub file and to the custom scripts located in /etc/grub.d. No changes are made to the GRUB 2 menu until the update-grub command is run as root, which runs the configuration scripts and updates the /boot/grub/grub.cfg file.

input.text: Should I install Ubuntu in UEFI mode or in legacy mode alongside an existing Windows install?
input.subject: Dual boot with Windows

expected.answer: Match whatever the other systems use. If the other systems on your computer are installed in UEFI mode then you must install Ubuntu in UEFI mode too; if they are installed in Legacy mode then you must install Ubuntu in Legacy mode too.

input.text: The package manager refuses to install anything and complains about packages with unmet dependencies. How do I fix it?
input.subject: apt reports unmet dependencies

expected.answer: Run apt-get check, a diagnostic tool that updates the package lists and checks for broken dependencies, then run apt-get -f install, which does the same thing as Fix Broken Packages in Synaptic when you get complaints about packages with unmet dependencies.

input.text: How do I add or temporarily disable a software repository from the command line?
input.subject: Add a software repository

expected.answer: Software repositories are listed in /etc/apt/sources.list, and by editing that file from the command line you can add, remove, or temporarily disable software repositories. Backup the configuration file first: sudo cp /etc/apt/sources.list /etc/apt/sources.list.backup.

input.text: A guide told me to add a PPA to get a newer version of a program. What is a PPA and is it safe?
input.subject: Is a PPA safe to use?

expected.answer: A PPA is a Personal Package Archive, a method of distributing software to users without requiring developers to undergo the full process of distribution in the main ubuntu repositories. PPAs have not undergone the same process of validation as regular ubuntu packages, so end users install PPAs at their own risk.

input.text: My printer is not detected at all. How do I get it working on Ubuntu?
input.subject: Printer is not detected

expected.answer: Install and maintain the printer using the tools for its manufacturer - there are pages for HP, Canon, Lexmark, Samsung and Xerox printers. Virtually all of the better models support PostScript and work very well, so take care buying low end printers of any brand.

input.text: After an update my nvidia graphics card fell back to a basic driver. How do I install the proprietary driver?
input.subject: Nvidia driver is not loading

expected.answer: The open source Nouveau driver lacks support for 3D acceleration, while the closed source NVIDIA drivers developed by NVIDIA provide excellent 3D acceleration and video card support. Install the nvidia-graphics-drivers package provided by the Ubuntu repositories that matches your version of Ubuntu and your graphics card.

input.text: Cheese does not display anything at all from my webcam. What should I check next?
input.subject: Webcam shows nothing

expected.answer: Try one of the other programs, such as Empathy, to make sure that Cheese is not causing the problem. Your media player may also need to know the video and audio device files for your webcam: before you plug in your webcam run ls /dev/video* and ls /dev/audio* at a console and note the difference.
